chapter: Jazz at the Philharmonic and the record business
title: The JATP with Bird and Prez
summary: On 'Lady Be Good' Bird outplays the others in 1946 so that nobody wants to follow him.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Going back to California, though, I wanted to talk about maybe what you remembered about that Jazz At The Philharmonic that you were on with Bird and Prez, where you did "I Can't Get Started" and "After You've Gone" and those things. Because Bird and Prez really didn't do that much together, and that was one of the few things they did.

Yeah. Well, at that time it was beautiful, because Bird was playing his heart out and so was Prez. I don't know how this came about, but I think that was made in 1948. I think it was '48 that they made that.
I think it was before that.
It was?
Yeah, I would think so.
Well, let's see. Jazz At The Philharmonic came out when, 1945?
Yeah. And this was probably when Bird was still in
California.
Yeah. Well, he came out there with Dizzy, you know.
And then the time with you and...
Yeah.
So I think that's when it was made. Because later he toured for Norman on Jazz at the Philharmonic, but this was...
When they did "Lady Be Good" and shit, that was bad! That was cut in '46.
"Lady Be Good," "I Can't Get Started," right. Al Killian.
Yeah, that's probably '46.
Willie Smith, yourself, Bird and Prez.

Yeah. I felt sorry for everybody after Bird got through playing. I said, "Pshew!" Because Al Killian and Willie Smith and them didn't know what Bird was playing. They didn't have the slightest idea. When Bird got through with it, I said, "Damn, man!" Because Prez didn't want to follow him. Prez followed him, man. Yeah, Prez followed him, but nobody wanted to follow him! Ha. And Willie Smith and those guys... If I was him, I would have said, "No, you've got it, man! You go ahead and play the tune. I don't need to play." Because really, he wasn't talking
about nothing when he got to whining on that saxophone. Because Charlie Parker was playing that son-of-a-bitch.
